clue.text: Concessionary agreement is to supplement concert income

annotationWithheld.why: Concessionary agreement is to supplement concert income (10): the parse is PROM+IS inside COME, which needs the single printed word 'income' to give both the container signal 'in' and the letters COME, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Concessionary agreement is to supplement concert income

clue.text: Muslim ruling half a state?

indicators.note: half signals that only the front five of the ten letters of the named state are kept

parts.note: California is a state of the USA

explanation.surface: A question about a religious judgement that applies to only part of a country.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half of CALIFORNIA gives the variant spelling of caliph; the question mark admits that CALIF is also the standard abbreviation for the state.
explanation.definitionFit: A calif is the ruling head of an Islamic state, successor to the Prophet as civil and religious leader.

clue.text: It's an omen, maybe, in North America

definitions.text: It's an omen, maybe, in North America

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters of the first three words could be another arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone sees a portent somewhere on the American continent.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines as well: rearrange ITSANOMEN and you get a state in North America.
explanation.definitionFit: Minnesota is a US state on the Canadian border, so it lies in North America.

clue.text: Disorderly hooligan outside British Library — untamed, unfortunately

parts.note: a rough is a rowdy, violent person, a hooligan

indicators.note: outside says the jumbled letters sit around the library's abbreviation
unfortunately suggests the word untamed has gone wrong and is jumbled

parts.note: BL is the standard abbreviation for the British Library in London

explanation.surface: A lout causes trouble at a national library, behaving wildly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' turns UNTAMED into ANDTUME, and 'outside' puts that round BL, giving ANDTUMBLE after ROUGH.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough-and-tumble describes a scrappy, chaotic scramble, so it means disorderly or lacking rules.

clue.text: When given horses, these troops are out of their element

definitions.text: When given horses, these troops are out of their element

parts.words: When given horses, these troops are out of their element
parts.note: sea-going soldiers put on horseback are the proverbial absurdity of the 'horse' variety, fighting men far from water

explanation.surface: Seaborne soldiers handed cavalry mounts would be hopelessly out of place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse marines' is an old joke phrase for an absurd or impossible corps, as in 'tell that to the horse marines'.
explanation.definitionFit: Marines are soldiers who serve from ships, whose natural element is the sea rather than the saddle.

clue.text: Girl carrying letter from abroad — one for a Japanese officer

indicators.note: carrying means the girl's name holds another piece within it

parts.note: Sara is a girl's name
mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet, so foreign
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A young woman brings a foreign letter addressed to a Japanese officer.
explanation.definitionFit: The samurai were the hereditary military class of feudal Japan, sword-bearing retainers who held officer rank.

clue.text: Cut off handle of whip

explanation.surface: An instruction to cut away the grip of a whip.
explanation.definitionFit: To crop is to cut short or trim; a riding crop is a short whip, and the crop is also the handle of a whip.

clue.text: Relation missed beginning and end of speech.

indicators.note: missed beginning and end of says the formal address loses its first and last letters

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: A relative failed to hear the start and finish of a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relation' looks like a family member; here it is the mathematical sense, proportion.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio is the quantitative relation between two amounts, such as three to one.

clue.text: Joke mildly, though with some piquancy

parts.note: a pun is a joke playing on words
gently means mildly

explanation.surface: Someone teases softly yet with a bit of bite.
explanation.definitionFit: Pungently means in a sharp, biting way, which is to say with a tang or piquancy.

clue.text: Our masthead is an indication of where we are going

definitions.text: an indication of where we are going

explanation.surface: The newspaper reflects that its own title points to the direction of society.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue appeared in The Times, whose masthead is the title of the newspaper itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The paper's printed name is literally its banner title; the phrase also means a portent revealing the trend of the age.

clue.text: A prominent churchman once dispelled our apathy

parts.note: Cosmo Lang was Archbishop of Canterbury from 1928 to 1942

indicators.note: dispelled means scattered, so the letters of the word our are scattered

explanation.surface: A notable cleric of the past drove away a congregation's indifference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispelled' turns OUR into UOR after LANG.
explanation.definitionFit: Languor is listless lethargy, a lack of energy or interest akin to apathy.

clue.text: Damp month in Paris turning clear

parts.note: mois is the French word for month

indicators.note: turning means the word for clear is read in the other direction

parts.note: net means clear, as in net profit after deductions

explanation.surface: A wet spell in a French month gives way to clear weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes TEN from NET. 'Damp' is a verb here: to make wet.
explanation.definitionFit: To moisten is to make slightly wet, which is to dampen.

clue.text: It may revitalize student coming out of Sorbonne finals

annotationWithheld.why: It may revitalize student coming out of Sorbonne finals (9): FRESHER around EN, but nothing in the clue gives EN in that order; Sorbonne's last two letters are NE and no word signals turning them
annotationWithheld.clue: It may revitalize student coming out of Sorbonne finals

clue.text: Bond's operation initially restricted by an informer

indicators.note: restricted by means one piece is held in by the informer's word

parts.note: a nose is slang for a police informer

indicators.note: initially selects the first letter of operation

explanation.surface: James Bond's mission is at first hemmed in by a grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' looks like the spy, but it is a tie or fastening; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a looped cord that binds, so it is a kind of tie or bond.

clue.text: Rugby boy in a reverie in his study?

definitions.text: in a reverie in his study?

explanation.surface: A schoolboy at a famous English school daydreams in his room.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Brown is the hero of Tom Brown's Schooldays, set at Rugby School in England; to be 'in a brown study' is to be lost in thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Brown is fiction's best-known Rugby pupil, and a 'brown study' is an idiom for a daydreaming trance.

clue.text: Ben's yell as "a cannon-ball took off his legs"?

definitions.text: Ben's yell as "a cannon-ball took off his legs"?

parts.words: Ben's yell as "a cannon-ball took off his legs"?
parts.note: Thomas Hood's comic poem about the soldier Ben, whose surname is a fight, who lost his legs to a cannon-ball; his shout is a war-shout

explanation.surface: A soldier screams as a cannon-ball strikes his legs.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Hood's ballad 'Faithless Nelly Gray' opens 'Ben Battle was a soldier bold... a cannon-ball took off his legs'.
explanation.definitionFit: A battle-cry is the shout soldiers raise when charging, and here also the cry of Ben Battle.

clue.text: Pelt a pirate — he's close enough!

parts.note: a skin is an animal's pelt
Captain Flint is the pirate in Treasure Island

explanation.surface: An urge to pelt a pirate who has come within range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' means stingy here, not nearby; 'enough' completes the surface joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A skinflint is a miser, and close is an old word for tight-fisted.

clue.text: Mysterious rites involving a priest — one of the elect

indicators.note: involving means the jumbled letters wrap round the following pieces
mysterious suggests the letters of rites are obscured into a new order

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: Secret ceremonies include a cleric, a member of the chosen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mysterious' turns RITES into ISRTE, and 'involving' puts A plus ELI inside it after ISR.
explanation.definitionFit: The Israelites are described in the Bible as God's chosen people.

clue.text: Fifth-columnist's idiosyncrasies take in most of the others.

indicators.note: take in means the quirks word holds another piece inside it

parts.note: traits are distinctive habits or idiosyncrasies

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the rest means the others

explanation.surface: A traitor's personal quirks absorb nearly everyone else's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' cuts REST to RES, which 'take in' puts inside TRAITS.
explanation.definitionFit: A fifth column is a group secretly working for the enemy, so one of its members is a female betrayer.

clue.text: Fugitive has space to manoeuvre with ease, we hear

indicators.note: to manoeuvre suggests the letters of space are moved around
we hear means the word ease is taken by its sound

parts.note: ease said aloud is the two-letter run of Es

explanation.surface: A runaway has room to get away comfortably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to manoeuvre' turns SPACE into ESCAP; 'ease' spoken sounds like 'Es', two letter Es.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapee is someone who has broken free, such as an escaped prisoner on the run.

clue.text: Look in the unfinished open area for dirt

indicators.note: in places the word for look inside the public space
unfinished means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a square is an open area in a town
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Searching a town plaza still under construction for grime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' trims SQUARE to SQUAR, around LO.
explanation.definitionFit: Squalor is filthy, wretched neglect, a state of dirt and grime.

clue.text: Trouble for Wharton at Greyfriars

explanation.surface: Some difficulty for a pupil at a fictional school.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Wharton is the leader of the Famous Five at Greyfriars School in Frank Richards' Billy Bunter stories.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry is to harass or pester; Harry is Wharton's first name in the school stories.

clue.text: Stand-in sounds dejected, with Latin coming next

indicators.note: sounds means the word for dejected is taken by how it is said

parts.note: low means dejected or down
cum is Latin for with

explanation.surface: A replacement seems miserable, and Latin follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a doctor or cleric temporarily covering for another, a substitute.

clue.text: Many a debtor appears to cringe

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, hence many
an ower is one who owes, a debtor

explanation.surface: A great many people in debt look ready to grovel.
explanation.definitionFit: To cower is to shrink back in fear, much as one cringes.

clue.text: Noble woman gives refuge to many — beyond enumeration

indicators.note: gives refuge to means the noblewoman shelters a piece inside

parts.note: a countess is a noblewoman
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, hence many

explanation.surface: A titled lady shelters countless refugees.
explanation.definitionFit: Countless means too many to be numbered, beyond counting.

clue.text: Spectacle which makes sense

explanation.surface: A display that is logical.
explanation.definitionFit: A sight is a spectacle worth seeing, and sight is one of the five senses.

clue.text: Plant fielder on firm wicket

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket
slip is a cricket fielding position beside the wicketkeeper

explanation.surface: A cricket instruction to station a fielder on a hard pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a verb meaning position; it is the definition, a wild flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The cowslip is a yellow-flowered wild primula of meadows.

clue.text: Rodent appears when girl loses article in heather

indicators.note: in means the shortened name sits inside the heather word

parts.note: ling is common heather

indicators.note: loses means a letter is taken away from the girl's name

parts.note: Emma is a girl's name
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A small animal shows up when a girl drops something in the heath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' strips A from EMMA to give EMM inside LING.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemming is a small Arctic rodent famed for its mass migrations.

clue.text: The thread of the story

parts.note: spun fibre for weaving, and also a tale told, so the plot line is both strand and narrative

explanation.definitionFit: Yarn is spun thread, and a yarn is also a long tale.

clue.text: In which one may look backward

definitions.text: In which one may look backward

parts.words: In which one may look backward
parts.note: a review of past events is a backward glance in time

explanation.definitionFit: Retrospect is a survey of the past, so in it one reviews earlier events.
